title: Mexican Political History Update — May 13, 2026
summary: A CNN investigation on May 12 revealed CIA operatives conducted covert lethal operations inside Mexico against cartels, triggering a new sovereignty crisis. Earlier, the US DOJ on April 29 indicted Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha (Morena) and nine officials on cartel conspiracy charges; Rocha resigned on May 2 — the first sitting Morena governor ousted under a US narco-trafficking indictment. On April 14, Mexico's Congress formally declared the Plan B electoral reform constitutional after 20 state legislatures ratified it, enacting changes to campaign finance, INE salaries, and party funding. Two new KPIs were added tracking the dismal 13% turnout in the June 2025 first-round judicial elections and the emergence of four new party formations seeking INE registration ahead of the 2027 midterms.

title: Breaking: Chamber of Deputies Passes Sheinbaum's 'Plan B' Electoral Reform 377–102
summary: Mexico's Chamber of Deputies approved President Claudia Sheinbaum's revised electoral reform ('Plan B') with 377 votes in favor and 102 against, backed by Morena and Movimiento Ciudadano.
